name: Gross Profit
description: Calculate gross profit as revenue minus cost of goods sold.
business_contexts: a retailer calculating gross profit after cost of goods sold
a manufacturer calculating gross profit on a product line
an e-commerce brand calculating gross profit after landed cost
a consumer goods company calculating gross profit across a quarter
a distributor calculating gross profit on a shipment
question_patterns: Given the revenue and cost of goods sold below, what is gross profit?
Calculate gross profit from the figures given.
What is gross profit, given the revenue and COGS shown below?
Calculate gross profit by subtracting COGS from revenue given.
Using the revenue and COGS below, what is gross profit?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate gross profit = revenue − cogs
key_insight: Gross profit only nets out the direct cost of producing what was sold — operating expenses like overhead and salaries still sit below it.
common_mistakes: Subtracting operating expenses along with COGS, which belongs at the operating profit line instead
Reporting COGS itself as if it were the gross profit figure
framework_soundbite: Gross profit is revenue minus COGS — nothing else has come out yet.
